results.summary: This combinational multiplier takes a 4-bit multiplicand and 4-bit multiplier and produces an 8-bit product. A signed_mode input selects whether the operands are treated as unsigned or signed using the Modified Baugh-Wooley algorithm. In unsigned mode the multiplier uses an array of full-adder and AND-gate cells, with a ripple-carry adder forming the upper product bits. It can be tested on a Tiny Tapeout demoboard by setting the switches and reading the product on a 7-segment display.

results.summary: This Verilog multimode modem performs digital modulation and demodulation using ASK, FSK, and PSK schemes. It uses a 10 MHz clock to generate digitized sinusoidal signals internally, and two selection inputs choose the modulation scheme. The modulated signal appears on mod_out pins and the recovered data appears on demod_out. Testing requires applying a 10 MHz clock, a reset pulse, and using selection inputs 01, 10, or 11 for ASK, FSK, or PSK respectively.

results.summary: This Verilog design is a 12-hour clock rendered as triangles using a race-the-beam triangle renderer. A state machine incrementally rasterizes three triangles from their edge equations while generating VGA timing, and each frame updates the second, minute, and hour hands from lookup tables. It uses the Tiny VGA pinout and requires a TinyVGA adapter and VGA monitor to view. Input pins advance the minute and hour hands, and the silicon-tested clock was confirmed to run on time and respond to adjustments.
